task.title: Execute selected worker models through engine-owned task attempts
task.goal:
## Latest installed interruption evidence

Published head e35283303f4c5823c612686d32fb6bee1ac368ac contains harness 2f7a1a34 and its actual BF16 interruption/recovery evidence. Exactly two real calls occurred; the engine was killed after the worker response reached the relay but before engine acceptance. Reopen and a separate credential-free recovery retained the same selector, reserved worker, original deadline and two spent steps. No accepted worker result, retry, capacity clearance or provider-termination claim. Four focused relay tests, compile/workflow checks, captured-byte manifest verification and documentation/inventory checks pass.

[Immutable result and raw receipts](https://github.com/rrflow/rrflow-development/blob/e35283303f4c5823c612686d32fb6bee1ac368ac/docs/evidence/change-journals/gate-g/task-worker-interruption-live.md). The installed primary remains c75c1896; no new engine or release bundle was built. Keep draft: remaining policy/credential acceptance and actual prerequisite landing precede ready-for-review and full candidate CI. Safe reconciliation/resume and the complete UI/project/RROFLOW/learning/release workflow remain open. Earlier briefs below retain their historical scope and starting observations.

## Outcome and ownership

An accepted SWAG routing proposal previously had no admitted selected-worker call. This change adds `task-worker-execute`: RRFlow resolves the retained choice and current task/configuration, authorizes the call, reserves effort and shared capacity, and retains bounded model draft text under guarded completion. Text acceptance does not mutate a project, complete a task or create a training label.

Driver: active SWAG session. G-01b/G-02a and POAM-009 own this increment; I-03/I-07 retain project effects and orchestration. Product version remains 1.0.0. This is a draft dependent on PR206 and the remaining native-client/startup/distribution chain. Public main through `906bec82` is ordinarily merged; no production source changed in that reconciliation. PR229 is not a release or full SWAG-completion claim.

## Implementation and boundaries

- One bounded HTTP model-content transport beneath the existing strict selector wrapper; explicit generation, response format, effort mapping and worker policy under the existing configuration approval digest.

- One engine-owned selected-worker operation using current task/selection/configuration/context authorization, the existing attempt/budget ledger, shared endpoint capacity and guarded completion. Unknown execution remains uncertain across reopen; it is not silently retried.

- Typed retained output, public catalogue/action/handler and generated SDK/OpenAPI projections. The Rust worker method uses one transport attempt and validates response identity. PR222 is ordinarily composed at `43d18059`; proposal and worker now share its catalogue-derived one-attempt carriage and contract-owned response validation. PR222 itself still requires protected landing.

- The existing installed proof runner gains explicit worker mode and credential-free recovery of both attempts. No additional execution authority or direct provider dispatcher.

No provider rankings, task-specific routes, endpoint URLs, model names or credentials are embedded in product behavior. Missing configuration or unsupported effort remains a denial. Historical context is not current filesystem freshness or mutation permission. Native Claude/Codex subscription adapters remain separate required work.

## Validation and retained failures

The native-client composition passed 189 contract/client tests, strict all-target/all-feature Clippy, 32 architecture checks, generated parity (72 operations/seven signals), formatting and repository checks. The retained real worker response is now a hash-checked conformance fixture; corruptions are explicit rejection probes, not training observations.

An exact-source native example at clean `43d18059` completed actual selector and worker calls against the separately identified `c75c1896` engine. Missing-credential denial, unchanged task state, restar
